output.methodChoice: EDF analysis, two catalogue items collected (X3 per-cell timing, X12 storage-node metrics)
output.brief:
The latency regression is most likely caused by the storage-node compaction tuning pushed through the fleet config system on the evening of 2 Nov (ticket FC-7710), not by gateway 5.8. In each cell, disk utilisation jumped to about 97% and node-side GET time rose from 61 to 262 ms within minutes of that push. Cell aps-3 was never pushed and stayed at about 94 ms even with 5.8 running. The one gateway rollback test (euw-1, 6 Nov) left p99 unchanged. Confidence is moderate-to-good, not certain: I did not read the change ticket itself, and the backlog's source is still unattributed until 10 Nov.

Do not roll back the gateway fleet-wide. It would not fix latency and would reopen the SEC-2291 replay weakness, with audit closure due 30 Nov. Do not pause compaction, since that risks disk-full nodes. Next, revert the compaction tuning in one cell, watch GET p99 and disk utilisation, then extend the revert if it recovers. Hold off on rate-limiting Orrin Media until the backlog attribution is in. Ask the gateway team to profile 5.8's CPU use before the next release.
